problems.title: A logarithmic inequality with base below one
problems.question: Solve log base sin25° of |2x−1| > log base sin25° of 3.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: 0<sin25°<1, so the logarithm reverses order; its argument must remain positive.
steps: Require 0<|2x−1|<3. The upper bound gives −1<x<2, while positivity excludes x=1/2.

problems.title: A radical factor creates an isolated solution
problems.question: Solve (x−4)√(log₃x−1)≥0.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: The domain is x≥3 and the radical is nonnegative.
steps: At x=3 the radical is zero, so this endpoint is a solution. For x>3 the radical is positive, requiring x−4≥0.
Thus the solution is {3} together with [4,∞).

problems.title: An exponential of a logarithm
problems.question: Solve $4^{\log_2x}+x^2<8$.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
steps: The inequality becomes 2x²<8. On the positive domain this is 0<x<2.

problems.title: Circumscribed cylinder of a regular hexagonal prism
problems.question: All edges of a regular hexagonal prism equal a. Find the volume of its circumscribed cylinder.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: A regular hexagon’s circumradius equals its side.
steps: The cylinder radius and height are both a. Thus V=πa²×a=πa³.

problems.title: A sphere through four regular-tetrahedron vertices
problems.question: Three chords of a sphere start at one point, each length 4, with pairwise angles 60°. Find sphere volume.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Cosine rule gives all other endpoint distances 4, so the four endpoints form a regular tetrahedron.
steps: A regular tetrahedron of edge s has circumradius s√6/4, obtained by locating the centroid on its height. Here R=√6.

problems.title: A planar logarithm system
problems.question: Shade log base (2−x) of (2−y)>0 and log base (4−y) of (2x−2)>0.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Both bases must be positive and not 1; both arguments positive.
steps: The arguments give y<2 and x>1. The first base then lies in (0,1), so its inequality requires 2−y<1, giving y>1. Also its base requires x<2.
Now 1<y<2 makes the second base >1. Its inequality requires 2x−2>1, or x>3/2.
The solution is the open rectangle 3/2<x<2,1<y<2, excluding all four edges.

problems.title: A triangular pyramid section through an edge midpoint
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has base side 6. A section through one base edge and midpoint of the opposite lateral edge has area 6√6. Find pyramid volume.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: The base altitude is 3√3; the apex projection is the centroid, distance √3 from the chosen base edge.
steps: The section vertex is midpoint M of the opposite lateral edge. Its planar projection is distance (3√3+√3)/2=2√3 from the chosen base edge, and its vertical height is H/2.
Section altitude=2(6√6)/6=2√6. Therefore (2√6)²=(2√3)²+H²/4, giving H=4√3.
The base area is 9√3 and volume=(9√3)(4√3)/3=36.

problems.title: Integer and fractional parts of a logarithm
problems.question: Solve floor((log₂x)³)+2floor((log₂x)²)−floor(log₂x)={log₂x}+2.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: The left side is an integer, so the fractional part on the right must be zero.
steps: Put t=log₂x. Then t is an integer, and the equation becomes t³+2t²−t−2=0.
It factors as (t+2)(t+1)(t−1)=0, giving t=−2,−1,1.
Exponentiating gives x=1/4,1/2,2, all valid.

problems.title: Three mutually tangent spheres on a plane
problems.question: Spheres touch a plane at the vertices of a 6,8,10 triangle and touch one another externally. Find their radii.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: For two spheres on the same side of a tangent plane, contact-point distance d satisfies d²=4rᵢrⱼ.
steps: Assign AB=6,BC=8,AC=10. Then r_A r_B=9,r_B r_C=16,r_A r_C=25.
Dividing products gives r_A=√(9×25/16)=15/4, r_B=12/5, r_C=20/3.
They must be on the same side: opposite-side centres would already have vertical separation rᵢ+rⱼ and nonzero horizontal separation, preventing contact.

problems.title: A logarithmic inequality true at every real input
problems.question: Find a such that 1+log₅(x²+1)≥log₅(ax²+4x+a) for every real x.
problems.idea: Use exact formulas and retain every domain, sign and existence condition.
formulas: Right argument must be positive everywhere, requiring a>2. Since base 5>1, compare the arguments after writing 1=log₅5.
steps: The inequality becomes (5−a)(x²+1)−4x≥0 for all x.
If c=5−a, the quadratic c x²−4x+c is everywhere nonnegative iff c≥2 (positive leading coefficient and discriminant 16−4c²≤0).
Thus a≤3. Combining with the strict logarithm-domain condition gives 2<a≤3.
